method: Deduplicate exact-build run/sequence/code. Restrict to each own-device CONNECTED-to-collection interval. Pair A source and B receiver only by unique exchange tag; only complete successful pairs enter latency summaries. Bitmasks identify measured durations. Never subtract clocks across devices. Exchange residual includes network plus endpoint scheduling, not pure RTT. Cadence includes user pauses.

baseline.scope: Descriptive older sample, different test and duration; not a controlled benchmark.

limitations: No observed recurrence in this finite interval is not proof of permanent resolution.
Dispatch measures software processing, not physical mouse-to-screen latency.
Profile retention is bounded; do not treat recorded frames as all physical events.
Incomplete historical control logs remain excluded from claims about missing events.
A/B local spans overlap and cannot simply be summed.

validation.collection: Both request-specific payloads parsed and hashed; exact-build deduplication and unique pairs asserted.
validation.tests: Not run: read-only diagnostics and report; no runtime changes.
validation.remoteCI: Not run: no code change or push.

findings.evidence: All 11 retained paired exchanges ended ok and complete. Both current protected services/input health are READY. Exact-build post-CONNECTED logs contain no fault/failure/timeout/reconnection events and only one connection run per side. Sampled source-worker heartbeat reply-gate waits are all below 1ms (A 14, B 17). This does not establish permanent reliability or exercise the prior 2s stalled-reader case.

Compared descriptively with g508 complete-pair samples, capture activation median is 12.988ms versus 34.6835ms, but maximum is 160.287ms versus 120.464ms. Receiver-ready maximum remains 275.330ms versus 273.876ms. Samples and observation durations differ; this is not a controlled improvement estimate.

9 paired receivers used preparation and 2 reported PreparationExpired. The expired entries have receiver ReadyWait of 275.330ms and 273.055ms. The worst source exchange wait is 291.039ms, with receiver-local request-handler-to-grant-write service of 283.969ms and residual 7.070ms. Residual includes network and endpoint scheduling; it is not pure RTT. The two expired samples have zero retransmitted bytes. One other matched sample reports 148 retransmitted bytes; all 11 measured TCP profiles have zero timeout episodes.
findings.nestedStages: Worst expired entry reports service bootstrap validation 148.838ms, native pair ready 111.327ms, and installation/self checks 62.437ms and 61.677ms. Native image-hash work is 54.269ms and 54.013ms. These local scopes overlap or occur before a warm claim and must not be added to ReadyWait.

findings.evidence: The worst capture activation is 160.287ms; its exact matching IPC response wait is 156.487ms and IPC authority check 3.286ms. Native queue-to-handler and foreground stages are each in the 10-100ms bucket; current buckets do not establish precise separate contributions or prove a single foreground API is the cause.

Worst B input dispatch is 48.755ms, all reported in client response wait; client lock and authority are measured zero. Matching worker buckets are authorization 2ms, scope 20ms, apply 25ms (quantized). The finer worker apply span is 25.536ms, including a single SendInput of 1.070ms. The entire 48.755ms cannot be attributed to the native injection syscall.
